newsitem.title: USA: Hartford Financial reports jump in earnings.
newsitem.headline: Hartford Financial reports jump in earnings.

text.p: Hartford Financial Services Group Inc. said Monday its operating earnings jumped 43 percent in the second quarter, aided by a strong performance in its life insurance business.
Hartford Financial said operating profits rose to $182 million, or $1.54 a share, for the quarter, from $127 million, or $1.08 a share, in the same period last year.
The results edged out Wall Street's average estimate of $1.50 a share, according to a survey conducted by First Call.
Revenues in the second quarter totalled $3.1 billion vs. $3.0 billion a year ago.
The operating results exclude a one-time gain of $368 million, along with $24 million in net realised capital gains.
Including the special items, Hartford Financial said it earned $574 million, or $4.86 a share, compared with $143 million, or $1.22 a share a year ago.
The net income includes a $368 million equity gain from the initial public offering on an 18.6 percent stake in the company's Hartford Life Inc. subsidiary.
Fuelling the jump in profits were strong showings by its life and North American property casualty insurance businesses and smaller losses from its catastrophe insurance unit, the company said.
But the growth was partially offset by weaker returns from the company's international operations.

"The successful execution of our basic strategies, coupled with favourable catastrophe experience and higher net investment income, were largely responsible for our healthy earnings," said Hartford Chairman Ramani Ayer.
"In spite of the very competitive and difficult market conditions, we had a strong performance during the quarter," he said.
Catastrophe losses fell to $3 million in the second quarter from $30 million a year ago.
In its life insurance business, second-quarter core earnings rose 68 percent to $74 million from $44 million a year ago.

In its international segment, core earnings fell 35 percent to $13 million in the second quarter from $20 million a year ago, primarily due to difficult conditions in the British automobile insurance market, the company said.
The company's stock rose 31 cents to $85.94 in midafternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
